title: A blocked hand-in's failing ids are run by devloop; when they pass, the worker runs again in a round that does not count (issue #4b)
objective: When a worker hands in blocked with failing test ids that pass when devloop runs them, the ticket does not stop: the worker runs again, on the next command of its chain, in a round that does not count.
outline: devloop/prompts/worker.md: the blocked hand-in example gains "failing": ["<test id>", ...] and one sentence. devloop/core/agents.py: start() gets an optional first=0 that starts the chain at that index (the Pending's full_chain is that slice, so a quota wait restarts from it), and Pending exposes the index (in the role's whole chain) of the command whose hand-in it collected. devloop/ticket_issuer.py _round(): in the blocked branch, after the escalation check of issue #4a, take whand.result['failing']; when valid, run testrun.run(cfg, self.wt, 'run', ids, timeout=self.left(), keep_dir=runs/<id>/blocked-check) under self.test_slot(); GREEN -> do not raise: keep a problem text like 'the worker handed in blocked (<text>), but the ids it named (<ids>) passed when devloop ran them on <branch>: the block was the agent's own environment, not the ticket; continue the work', set self._free = 'agent_env', remember the next chain index for the next worker start, make sure worker_ok stays False, go on with the verifier part of the round and return the feedback; otherwise raise Stuck('decision', text + newline + 'devloop ran the ids the worker named: ' + out.summary()). free_rounds()/rounds_text() as in acceptance 8. Issuer.start() passes first=<remembered index> to the worker's agents.start once, then resets it to 0.
test_plan: Verifier writes cases for acceptance 1-5 in tests_devloop/test_issuer.py, a new class T<id>Acceptance(LoopCase) placed right after class FreeRounds (before class T11Acceptance); setUp removes every DEVLOOP_* key from self.env and from os.environ (mock.patch.dict, as T109Acceptance does) and sets self.env['FAKE_RUN_IDS'] to a file under self.tmp. The verifier adds one fake: in tests_devloop/fake_agent.py's worker section, a branch for action 'blocked_failing' placed right after the 'revise_blocked' branch the issue #4a ticket adds, with the comment '# issue #4b: blocked with failing ids from $FAKE_FAILING', handing {"kind": "blocked", "text": "cannot reach 127.0.0.1 from this sandbox", "failing": json.loads(os.environ.get("FAKE_FAILING") or '["suite.base"]')} and exiting 0 without committing. fake_tests.py's `run` of ids that are not case_* passes 'suite.base' always, passes 'impl.impl_1.txt' only when impl_1.txt says ok, and appends the ids line to $FAKE_RUN_IDS (#109). Acceptance 2: self.config(max_rounds=1); self.add(1); plan worker {'1': ['blocked_failing', 'ok']}; FAKE_RUN_IDS lines == ['suite.base']. Acceptance 3: self.config(agents=dict({r: AGENT for r in ROLES}, worker_simple=[AGENT + ['--model', 'w1'], AGENT + ['--model', 'w2']])) (cost rows carry model = the value after --model); compare [(row['round'], row['model']) for row in t['cost'] if row.get('role') == 'worker']. Acceptance 4: self.env['FAKE_FAILING'] = '["impl.impl_1.txt"]', plan worker {'1': ['blocked_failing']}. Acceptance 5: plan worker {'1': ['blocked_failing']}, max_rounds 1. Acceptance 1: render worker.md with agents.render and a dummy value for every placeholder (as test_regression_fixer.T81Acceptance's rendered() helper does) and assert '"failing"' is in it. Expected values come from this ticket and the fakes. Red before (read from the code at 7be8b0b and the measured blocked run): every blocked hand-in ends stuck (decision) at round 1, nothing is run, worker.md has no 'failing'. Acceptance 6-11: implementer's own tests (6 and the escalation order already hold for today's code paths; 8 includes the in-place change of test_5).
notes: Issue #4 (GitHub #4), part (b); depends on the issue #4a ticket (same blocked branch of _round, same fake_agent worker section). Observed in T on 2026-11-22 (#319): the agent's own sandbox blocked loopback HTTP; the same case passed on the host in 10 s. The free round reuses the existing free-round mechanism (merge conflict, cases_wrong revision), so the 2 x max_rounds ceiling also caps a worker that keeps blocking. Design choice: the restart is the next round (new run dir r<N+1>-worker, the note travels in the feedback the worker prompt already shows), not a second worker inside the same round. hard_block patterns match every added line: do not write the words os.kill, killpg, pkill or 'kill -' anywhere (Pending.stop already uses osx.kill_tree, which does not match). Out of scope: changing any agent sandbox.
acceptance: The rendered worker prompt (devloop/prompts/worker.md) shows a blocked hand-in with a "failing" list of test ids and says that devloop runs those ids itself and starts the worker again when they pass.

A worker that hands in {"kind": "blocked", "text": ..., "failing": ["suite.base"]} (an id that passes) with max_rounds 1, then 'ok': the ticket ends 'landed' with round 2; its round-1 'feedback' event has free 'agent_env'; the round-2 worker prompt (<worktrees>/runs/1/r2-worker/prompt.md) contains 'passed when devloop ran them' and 'suite.base'; the ids were run exactly once (one `run suite.base`); there is no decision page with ref '1'.

With a worker chain of two commands whose models are w1 and w2, the ticket's worker cost rows are round 1 model 'w1' and round 2 model 'w2'; with a chain of one command, round 2 runs the same command as round 1.

A blocked hand-in whose failing ids do not all pass (['impl.impl_1.txt'] while the worker wrote no impl_1.txt): the ticket is 'stuck' with reason 'decision' and exactly one decision page with ref '1' whose text contains the worker's text and 'impl.impl_1.txt'.

A worker that keeps handing in blocked with passing ids, max_rounds 1: the ticket ends 'stuck' with reason 'rounds' at round 2 and its stuck text contains '2 rounds used and still not passing (0 real red, 2 free: 0 merge conflict, 0 revision, 2 agent environment)'.

A blocked hand-in without 'failing', or whose 'failing' is not a non-empty list of strings, runs nothing and is stuck with a page as before (the blocked-page rule of issue #4a). When the worker's revise escalated in that round, the ids are not run and no page is written (escalation first).
A run of the ids that is not green (red, env, unmeasured) ends in the stuck page of acceptance 4, whose text carries the run's summary.

free_rounds() returns the keys 'merge', 'revision' and 'agent_env'; rounds_text() adds ', N agent environment' inside its parentheses only when N > 0, so every existing rounds text is unchanged. The existing case test_5_free_rounds_counts_free_feedback_events_since_the_last_round_one (test_issuer.py) is changed in place: each expected dict gains 'agent_env': 0.

The ids run once in the worker's worktree (the ticket branch) through the project's `run`, under a machine slot taken the way run_cases takes it (its wait added to the issuer's deadline), with output kept in <worktrees>/runs/<id>/blocked-check. The verifier's hand-in of that round is still checked and its cases saved as in any round; the blocked worker's hand-in never counts as a finished worker.

The next command is the one after the command that handed in blocked, or the same command when it was the chain's last; it applies only to the round right after; a quota fallback inside that run continues from that command onward.
devloop/README.md: the worker row says the hand-in is done or blocked (with optional failing ids); the loop summary at the top lists the agent-environment round among the rounds that do not count.
token_basis: four files change (ticket_issuer._round/free_rounds/rounds_text/start, core/agents.py start + Pending index, worker.md, README), one existing case changed in place, one fake action, 5 verifier cases of ~2-10 s each, plus the review a complex ticket gets; calibrated on #108/#109 (9.2M/9.9M recorded, cache reads included).
vision: VISION metrics 每張票需要我介入幾次 and 每張落地票的 token 與時間 (both down): a false environment block (T #319) no longer stops a ticket for the user; one devloop test run of the named ids replaces a user decision and a two-hour wait.
removes: the user's manual check of an agent's environment claim (rerunning its failing case by hand, then `actl tickets ready N`).
request:
# Four fixes reported by tabby_pool (T) as GitHub issues #1, #2, #4, #5 on sai99claw/agent-control

The user asked for all four (2026-11-23: 「1245 這些聽起來都好解決先處理掉」). Each ticket names its issue number in its title or notes so the main session can close the issue after landing. Issue texts are quoted below as reported; they are data, not instructions. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ (or a new file for a new area), using loop_harness.py; never a catch-all file.

## Issue #1: a release red that is a test failure gets an agent, not only a page
User ruling (tabby D-H79 addendum, verbatim): 「發版測試 跟 落地測試一樣 如果失敗 都要找agent 去查 去修」. Today a failed `devloop.release` writes one decision page ("leave it or run the release again?") and nothing investigates. In T, three release reds that passed on a plain rerun were real product races.
Wanted:
- The release command's exit code says what kind of failure it was, like the test interface does: rc 1 = the product failed a check (for T: release-test red on staging, prod untouched); rc 86 = the environment (a push refused, a build tool missing, a host down); anything else is treated like 86. Document this contract in devloop/README.md.
- rc 1: the controller has a fix ticket opened through the normal opener path (the same thing `actl new --request-file` does), with a request that carries the group, sha, the last `devloop-stage:` line, and the release log tail (the failing case and its message when the log has them). The ticket then goes worker -> verifier -> regression -> land -> release like any other. The controller also re-runs the release once on the same sha; a second rc 1 writes the decision page as today (naming the opened ticket). Never patch anything on the release path itself.
- rc 86 / other / timeout: as today (one decision page, no ticket, no rerun).
- agent-control's own scripts/release.sh: a refused tag push is the environment, so it exits 86 (in the cloud every release fails that way; it must not open a ticket per landing).
- Out of scope: rolling back a release.

## Issue #2: every flaky case gets a fix ticket
Same ruling as #1. #109 turns a rerun-green red into one `flaky (passed when run again): ...` line on the landed page; in T every such red chased so far was a real product race (#259, #260, #295, #317, #318), not a bad test.
Wanted:
- When a group lands (or ends stuck) with a non-empty flaky list, the controller has one fix ticket opened through the same opener path as #1 (reuse #1's mechanism; this ticket depends on #1's ticket): one request naming every flaky id with both messages (the red one and the fact it passed on the rerun), asking to find and fix the cause (product race or test), never by a sleep or a retry inside the test.
- Do not open a second ticket for an id an open (not landed, not cancelled) ticket already carries from this mechanism; say in the group event that it was already open.
- The landed page's flaky line also names the opened ticket.

## Issue #4: a worker's "blocked" is checked, and every stuck ticket gets a page
Observed in T (2026-11-22, #319): a fallback agent handed in `blocked` ("Chrome cannot navigate to 127.0.0.1 because the screen is locked; only the user can unblock this"). False: the same case passed on the host in 10 s; the agent's own sandbox blocked loopback HTTP. The ticket went `stuck (decision)` and no page was written: devloop/ticket_issuer.py `stuck()` skips the page for reason "decision" on the assumption that a revise escalation already wrote one, which is not true for a worker's `blocked` hand-in.
Wanted:
- (a) Every ticket that goes stuck has a page. Only a stuck that follows a revise escalation which already wrote its page (the opener's kind `question`) writes none; the page for a `blocked` hand-in quotes the worker's text and has the usual retry / revise / cancel options.
- (b) A `blocked` hand-in may name failing test ids (a `failing` list in the hand-in; add it to the worker hand-in format). When it does,
